Thanks for flagging, Marissa — and thanks Julia for the quick reply. A few points and next steps from collections/leadership perspective: 

1) Do not accept a partial/net payment without a signed agreement that the outstanding VAT will be paid if the certificate does not justify reversal. We have seen net-payments create reconciliation gaps.
2) Collections should send the standard 14-day notice for past due balance (per our policy) and place Novaris on credit hold immediately. That will preserve our leverage while they provide docs.
3) If Novaris provides a valid VAT certificate, we will reverse the VAT and issue a corrected invoice promptly. If they fail to provide evidence within 14 calendar days we proceed with escalation to final notice and service restriction per the contract.

Vivek — tagging you for visibility. If leadership wants to approve an exception to accept a short-term net payment (to avoid service disruption for a strategic account) please confirm. Otherwise Collections should proceed.

I'm attaching the final-notice template and a short checklist for VAT validation.

Attachments: final_notice_invoice_6782.pdf (pdf)
